nonfinite.construction: In the northern teachers’ construction 3.4.19 allows the exchange to carry the absolutive although it occurs after asking. 3.4.21 also permits the ordinary earlier-action construction.

nonfinite.allomorphy: Before lyap, 6.4.69 blocks general ī and 6.4.70 optionally supplies short i specifically to mayate. Short i licenses tuk and hence apamitya; retention of ā gives apamāya. The class-three measuring root is separately exemplified in pramāya.

taddhita.āpamityaka: Apamitya + kak as the first input in 4.4.21. The i-bearing lexicalized gerund is cited by name. No corresponding āpāmāyaka is claimed.
taddhita.yācitaka: Yācita + kan as the second input. Its final letters converge on -ka although the prescribed affixes have different markers.
taddhita.syntax: The Nyāsa explicitly allows the indeclinable first base despite the instrumental semantic government of the derivation. The Kaumudī shows the second with yācitena.

source.work: Śrīharṣa, Naiṣadhīyacarita 7.56, Sanskrit verse, second line
